options.text: The iron paper clip in the open saucer of water can rust because air and water both reach the iron.
The iron paper clip on the dry shelf will rust because air alone is enough.
The aluminium paper clip in the open saucer will develop brown rust like iron.
The oil coating on the third iron paper clip is itself rust.

stem:
Sana keeps one iron paper clip on a dry indoor shelf. She leaves a second iron paper clip in a saucer of water open to air. She coats a third iron paper clip with oil. She also has an aluminium paper clip in the same open saucer.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Iron rusts only when both air and water contact it; dry air alone is not enough, aluminium does not form brown iron rust, and oil is a coating that can block air and water, not rust.
